name: School Cleaning Checklist
description: A janitorial routine for cleaning classrooms, restrooms and common areas in a school.

items.text: Empty all trash and replace liners.
Disinfect desks, tables and chair surfaces.
Wipe down high-touch points like door handles and switches.
Clean the whiteboard or chalkboard and tray.
Sweep and mop or vacuum the floor.
Tidy supplies and straighten furniture.
Clean and disinfect all toilets and urinals.
Scrub and sanitize sinks and faucet handles.
Restock soap, paper towels and toilet paper.
Empty trash and sanitary bins.
Mop floors with disinfectant.
Wipe mirrors, partitions and door handles.
Wipe and disinfect all tables and benches.
Sweep and mop the dining and serving floors.
Clean and sanitize serving and counter surfaces.
Empty and sanitize trash and recycling bins.
Wipe down high-touch points and seating.
Check for spills and sticky residue under tables.
Sweep and mop hallways and entryways.
Disinfect handrails, lockers and water fountains.
Empty trash bins in shared spaces.
Clean entry glass and high-touch doors.
Wipe down office and reception surfaces.
Spot-clean walls and remove visible marks.
Scrub and machine-clean hard floors.
Dust vents, blinds and high surfaces.
Wash interior windows and glass.
Deep-clean and descale restrooms.
Disinfect shared keyboards and devices.
Inspect and refill all supply stations.

faq.q: What should be cleaned daily in a school?
faq.a: Daily tasks include emptying trash, disinfecting high-touch surfaces like door handles and desks, cleaning and restocking restrooms, sweeping and mopping high-traffic floors, and wiping down the cafeteria. These keep germs in check during the busiest hours.

faq.q: Which surfaces matter most for stopping illness?
faq.a: High-touch points spread germs fastest: door handles, light switches, desks, shared keyboards, faucet handles, and railings. Disinfecting these frequently, especially during cold and flu season, does more to reduce illness than scrubbing rarely-touched areas.

faq.q: How do I split daily and weekly cleaning tasks?
faq.a: Handle hygiene-critical work, like restrooms, trash, and high-touch surfaces, every day. Reserve deeper jobs, such as floor scrubbing, dusting vents, washing windows, and detailed restroom care, for a weekly rotation so they get done without overloading any single shift.

faq.q: How should cleaning supplies be stored?
faq.a: Keep all chemicals labeled, sealed, and locked away from students in a dedicated closet. Follow the dilution and contact-time instructions on each product, keep safety data sheets accessible, and ensure staff have the right protective gear.

faq.q: Is this school cleaning checklist available as a printable PDF?
faq.a: Yes. You can print it or download it as a PDF to post in the custodial closet for staff, then tick off each daily and weekly task to keep the campus consistently clean.
